items.title: Nortilus week 47: LR2 earnings down 30% w/w, VLCC down 18%
items.summary: Nortilus's Nov 20 weekly update puts VLCC earnings down 18% on the week at about $293k/day and LR2 earnings down 30%, while Aframax earnings rose 28%. Listed product tanker equities fell 7.2% on the week and are down 17.3% month to date; crude tanker shares fell 4.3% (−17.0% MTD).

items.title: Makai week 47: clean tanker earnings down 4.8% w/w, 13.4% off late-Oct peak
items.summary: Makai Research reports clean product tanker spot earnings fell 4.8% on the week, with Atlantic MRs taking most of the decline while Pacific MRs held near early-October highs; LRs slipped 2.1%. It cites a wider US Gulf ballast incentive and weak USG arbitrage as pressure on Atlantic MR balances, and notes the Aframax discount to LR2 above $100k/day is pulling some dirty LR2s into clean trades.

items.title: Gibson: refining margins weaken, led by gasoline
items.summary: Gibson's weekly report notes refining margins fell sharply over the month, with gasoline the weakest product and Asian gasoline cracks just above $1/bbl. Regional detail is in the full report.

items.title: Banchero Costa: Arabian Gulf crude exports down 27.6% Jan–Oct
items.summary: Using LSEG tracking, Banchero Costa puts Jan–Oct Arabian Gulf crude exports at 531.3 mt, down 27.6% y/y, cutting the region's share of global loadings to 30.6% from 39.8%. Global crude loadings fell 5.8% to 1,738.8 mt, while US exports rose 8.5% to 166.4 mt and South America 32.5% to 238.8 mt; China's imports fell 20.1%.

items.title: Hanwha Philly starts first Jones Act MR chemical/product tanker
items.summary: Hanwha Shipping began construction of the first of four 49,500 dwt MR oil/chemical tankers at Hanwha Philly Shipyard, designed for Jones Act trade with IMO Type II/III notation and an optional 18-segregation Type II layout; deliveries are due 2029–2030. Hanwha calls it the first US-built MR in nearly a decade.

items.title: MEPC 85 (Nov 30–Dec 3) to revisit IMO Net-Zero Framework
items.summary: The Baltic Exchange previews MEPC 85 in London, where the Net-Zero Framework approved in April 2025 remains unresolved after adoption was adjourned for a year in October 2025. Environmental groups want it adopted unchanged; the Union of Greek Shipowners has criticised the EU position.

items.title: Hafnia due to say by Nov 25 how it will handle its TORM stake
items.summary: After TORM rejected its merger proposals, Hafnia must disclose by Nov 25 whether it distributes its roughly 19.8% TORM stake (about 20.4m A shares, one TORM share per 26.3 Hafnia shares) or pays a cash dividend equal to 90% of Q3 net profit. TORM's $1.35/share interim dividend is payable Dec 2.

items.title: UKMTO: tanker in incident with military forces in Gulf of Oman
items.summary: UKMTO said on Sunday evening (Nov 22) that a tanker was involved in an incident with military forces in the Gulf of Oman near Chabahar, east of Hormuz and close to the US blockade line; investigations are ongoing and the vessel and forces involved were not identified. Separately, Iranian media said two supertankers caught fire after hitting mines east of the strait; this has not been independently confirmed.

items.title: Two more tankers hit near Khasab; UKMTO counts 106 incidents since Feb 28
items.summary: On Nov 21 an outbound VLCC (identified by Vanguard Tech as the Hong Kong-flagged Torkel) was hit in the stern about 11 nm north of Khasab and its crew evacuated, and the Suezmax Arina was hit in the engine room about 17 nm east of Khasab, starting a fire; no casualties were reported. UKMTO counted six tankers attacked in the week to Nov 18 and Hormuz transits fell to 263 from 308; JMIC rates the threat as severe. Iran's claim that a tanker struck a mine has not been verified.

items.title: Iran says ships must use its designated Hormuz lanes
items.summary: Citing Iran's armed forces, about 25 tanker-related incidents have occurred since Nov 14, roughly three a day. Tehran says vessels must coordinate with Iranian authorities and follow lanes it sets, warning non-compliant ships risk attack or mines.

items.title: TankerTrackers: AIS signal of Iranian 'blockade-runner' tanker was spoofed
items.summary: MarineTraffic data appeared to show an Iranian tanker named Khat-Shekan transiting Hormuz, but TankerTrackers says the vessel does not exist and satellite imagery does not corroborate the track. More than 14 tankers are reported gathered off Kharg Island; the US says its blockade of Iranian ports reached 130 consecutive days on Nov 21.

items.title: Houthis threaten Red Sea ports after coalition strikes Hodeidah
items.summary: The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted three ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh early Nov 21, after its Nov 20 operation hit Hodeidah port and depots in Sanaa. The Houthis have threatened Jeddah and other Saudi Red Sea ports.

items.title: Maersk/Hapag-Lloyd shift three more Gemini services back to Suez
items.summary: AE2 returns to the Suez routing from Dec 4, AE3 from Dec 20 and AE1 from Jan 14, 2027, following earlier moves for AE5, AE11, AE12, ME2 and ME1. The carriers say further changes depend on security conditions.

items.title: Houston Ship Channel pilot indicted over 2024 Lynchburg collision
items.summary: A Houston pilot was indicted for seaman's manslaughter over the July 19, 2024 collision between the bulker Yangze 7 and towboat Miss Peggy near Lynchburg; initial appearance is set for Nov 24. The allegations have not been proven.

items.title: Friday Nov 20 close: S&P 500 6,910.39 (−3.7%), Dow 48,147.33, Nasdaq 22,617.73
items.summary: In the latest completed session (Friday Nov 20) the S&P 500 fell 3.7% to 6,910.39, the Dow lost 949.73 pts (−1.93%) to 48,147.33 and the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.28% to 22,617.73, with the Nasdaq-100 down 5.6% as technology shares led the decline. For the week the Dow fell 8% (its worst week since March 2020), the S&P 500 8.6% and the Nasdaq about 10%. US markets reopen today, Monday Nov 23.

items.title: Brent settles $92.57 (+0.6%), WTI $83.98 Friday; third weekly loss
items.summary: Brent January rose $0.59 (+0.64%) to $92.57 and WTI December 0.93% to $83.98 on Nov 20, but both fell for a third week (Brent −3.4%, WTI −5.2% per FinanceFeeds; other sources differ on weekly %). Hormuz crude flows near pre-war levels weigh on prices; OPEC+ meets Nov 29 on 2027 quotas.

items.title: US natural gas near $3.30/MMBtu, third weekly gain
items.summary: Henry Hub futures traded around $3.30/MMBtu on Nov 20, on track for a weekly gain above 3% after an 11-month high of $3.372 on Nov 18. EIA reported a 20 bcf storage build vs 27 bcf expected; inventories are 2.1% above normal. Exact settle not confirmed.

items.title: Fed's Cook warns larger hikes may be needed later; 10-yr at 4.92%
items.summary: Governor Cook said in Santiago on Nov 20 that falling behind could require larger rate increases later, estimating October PCE at 3.8% and core 3.2%; fed funds is 3.75–4.00%. Futures price about 92% odds of a 25 bp hike Dec 8–9. The 10-year yield ended Friday at 4.92%, down 23 bp on the week.

items.title: Bessent urges Fed against a 50 bp hike
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Bessent told CNBC on Nov 20 he would urge the Fed not to raise rates by 50 bp, citing the energy shock and falling crude. CME FedWatch showed over 98% odds of a 25 bp move.

items.title: Monday pre-open: US futures higher, Kospi −3.2%, Tokyo closed; dollar index 103.6
items.summary: Early Nov 23, S&P 500 futures were up 2.1%, Nasdaq-100 futures 3.0% and Dow futures 1.4%. Japan was closed for a holiday after the Nikkei's 5.1% fall Friday; the Kospi fell 3.2% to about 4,716 while Taiwan's Taiex rose 2.4%. The dollar index eased 0.15% to 103.6 from a 19-month high, with EUR/USD at 1.0996 and USD/JPY at 158.94; Brent was near $90 and WTI near $83.4 (approximate).

items.title: Week ahead: PCE, GDP Wednesday; markets shut Thanksgiving
items.summary: Wednesday Nov 25 at 7:30 CT brings October PCE, the second Q3 GDP estimate and durable goods. Flash PMIs come Monday and consumer confidence Tuesday. US markets close Thursday for Thanksgiving and close early (noon CT) Friday.

items.title: NATO council meets Monday on Russian missiles that landed in Poland
items.summary: Two suspected Russian missiles, one identified as a Kh-101 cruise missile, and a suspected drone crashed in southeastern Poland on Nov 20 during a large Russian attack on Ukraine; no injuries were reported. NATO Secretary-General Rutte pledged to defend Polish territory, and the North Atlantic Council meets in Brussels on Nov 23; Poland has requested more early-warning aircraft and F-35s.

items.title: Iran says Hormuz shipping can resume quickly if US meets its terms
items.summary: Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said on Nov 23 that safe navigation could be restored quickly if the US lifts sanctions and its naval blockade and meets other terms of the June memorandum; talks remain stalled. Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Qatar condemned a Nov 21 Iranian attack on Bahrain that injured two people and started a fire at an industrial site in Sitra. An IRGC claim to have downed a US MQ-1 drone was not confirmed by CENTCOM.

items.title: Ballistic strike on Kryvyi Rih kills 2, wounds 60
items.summary: A Russian ballistic missile attack on Zelensky's hometown late Nov 20 killed two people and wounded 60, including six children, damaging about 25 apartment buildings and a hospital.

items.title: COP31 talks in Antalya run into second day of overtime
items.summary: UN climate negotiators in Antalya remained divided over language on phasing out fossil fuels on Nov 22, the second day past the scheduled close, as the Turkish presidency put forward a late compromise proposal. The EU presidency said chances of a deal were narrowing.

items.title: Finland reports drone strike on Russian cargo ship in Gulf of Finland
items.summary: Finnish authorities say drones hit a Russian cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland; details have not been confirmed. Mongolia is also heading to a snap presidential vote.

items.title: Broncos beat Raiders 38–24, improve to 8–2; at Steelers Friday
items.summary: Denver rallied from a 17–0 deficit on Nov 22; Jonah Coleman ran for 111 yards and Ja'Quan McMillan's 35-yard interception return for a touchdown sealed it. Bo Nix was 19 of 35 for 225 yards, 1 TD and 1 INT; the Raiders fell to 4–7. Next: at Pittsburgh on Black Friday, Nov 27 (kickoff time not confirmed in the source). AFC West standing after Week 12 not stated in the source.

items.title: Texans 4–6, second in AFC South; host Ravens Nov 29
items.summary: Houston beat Indianapolis 26–3 on Nov 19 for its first home win and sits second in the AFC South behind Jacksonville (7–2). DE Chris Braswell was carted off with a knee injury on the opening kickoff; no diagnosis yet. Next: Ravens (4–6) at Houston, Sunday Nov 29, CBS (kickoff listed as noon CT, unconfirmed).

items.title: Alcaraz beats Zverev 6-2, 7-6 to win first ATP Finals title
items.summary: Alcaraz went 5–0 in Turin and beat world No. 1 Zverev in 2 hours 1 minute on Nov 22 for his sixth title of 2026 and 30th overall (ATP gives the tiebreak score inconsistently). Zverev finishes the year at No. 1 with 10,350 points; Alcaraz closed to within 350 points of No. 2 Sinner, who missed the event injured.

items.title: Davis Cup Final 8 in Bologna, Nov 24–29
items.summary: Quarterfinals: Czechia–Canada Tue 9 AM CT, Italy–Korea Wed 9 AM CT, Great Britain–Germany Thu 3 AM CT and Austria–Spain Thu from 10 AM CT. Final is Sunday Nov 29 at 8 AM CT (schedule published in September).
